items.prompt: Given a sorted array and a key, return the index of the smallest element that is greater than or equal to the key.
items.why: Sorted + a single position next to a value (the ceiling) → binary search, and return lo when the range empties. Two pointers is for pairs.

items.prompt: An ascending array of distinct numbers was rotated at an unknown index. Find a target in O(log n).
items.why: Sorted in pieces + O(log n) → modified binary search: one half around mid is always sorted, so range-check that half.

items.prompt: Given a sorted array and a target, find two numbers that add up to the target.
items.why: A pair in a sorted array → opposite-end pointers, O(n). Binary searching a partner for each element is O(n log n).

items.prompt: Return the k numbers closest to x from an unsorted array.
items.why: Unsorted + 'k closest' → a size-k heap keyed by distance. Binary search needs sorted input (with a sorted array, binary search + a window would work).

items.prompt: Given a non-negative integer x up to 2³¹ − 1, return the floor of its square root without using a sqrt function.
items.why: Find the largest m with m·m ≤ x, and the test is monotonic in m → binary search on the answer range [0, x].

items.prompt: An array strictly increases and then strictly decreases. Find its maximum in O(log n).
items.why: Bitonic + O(log n) → compare nums[mid] with nums[mid+1] to tell which side of the peak you're on, and use the lo < hi form.

items.prompt: An array of n numbers holds values from 1 to n with exactly one missing and one repeated. Find both in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
items.why: Values in 1..n + unsorted + O(1) space → cyclic sort places each value at its index and reveals the mismatch. Sorting first to binary search costs O(n log n).

items.prompt: Given k sorted lists, find the smallest range that includes at least one number from each list.
items.why: Several sorted lists processed together → a min-heap of the current head of each list (k-way merge), tracking the current max.
